conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. On the positive side, record ARC/PLC cash reached farmers in October and Purdue's capital-investment index jumped from 39 to 55, both landing just before Titan's year-end selling season, and the options market is paying for upside (skew -11). On the negative side, December corn fell about 19% from its late-August high, consensus Q3 revenue sits at the top of the company's own guide-implied range, and the last three prints were sold. So p_up is 51 on a 13% absolute move; findings sum to +0.8, and the scaled number is a near-zero +0.26.
bar: Q3 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-10-31) consensus: EPS -$0.08 on revenue about $552.1M (Earnings Whispers/finviz preview, 2026-11-16, https://finviz.com/news/423386/titan-machinerys-rally-meets-a-tough-second-half-ag-test-as-europe-weakens), and Northland -$0.08. Benzinga shows -$0.06 on $541.2M and Earnings Whispers $556.2M (search snippet, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TITN/earnings-forecasts). Two estimate sources roughly agree. The company's FY27 guide is adjusted diluted EPS -$1.25 to -$1.75 and adjusted EBITDA $17-29M (reaffirmed 2026-08-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001409171/000162828026059170/afy27q2ex991earningsrelease.htm). H1 EPS was -$0.95 (-0.55 and -0.40), so the guide implies H2 of -$0.30 to -$0.80. FY consensus is -$1.50 (midpoint) on about $2.13B revenue. Segment guide applied to FY26 segment revenue gives FY27 of about $2.01-2.15B; at the end management leaned to, Q3 comes out around $520-540M.
positioning_check: Short interest was about 1.09M shares with 4.7 days to cover at the 2026-10-22 settlement (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=TITN, search snippet; MarketBeat returned 403). It was 873.9K / 3.89 DTC on 2026-06-30 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/titn/), so it has risen modestly. This is not a crowded short; % of float was not computed because the share count was not sourced. Options (baseline): event-implied move 15.37%, 25-delta skew -11.06 vol points (calls bid, upside paid), put/call OI 1.33 on only 1,206 contracts total, ATM spread 15% of mid, so the chain is thin. Tape: spot $20.70, -5.6% over 5 days, -10.3% over 20 days, 21% below the 52-week high. The finviz preview put the stock at $22.57 on 2026-11-16, about 16% below its post-earnings high of $26.90.

findings.finding: USDA put 2025-crop ARC/PLC payments at a record $13.8B gross, certified and paid in October 2026 (farmdoc projects about $13.2B net; corn $4.7B, wheat $2.9B, soybeans $1.5B). Separately, Purdue/CME's Farm Capital Investment Index for October 2026 jumped from 39 to 55, its highest in nearly a year, though only 20% of farmers said it is a good time to buy machinery. Both land just before Titan's Q4 (Nov-Jan), the year-end Section 179 buying season for its ND/SD/MN/MT/IA/NE wheat-corn-soy footprint. On 2026-08-27 management guided Q4 'a little stronger than Q3', and Q3 is the release where it typically updates the year-end outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the Q3 FY26 print (2025-11-25) the stock rose +18.5% on a surprise profit and a raised inventory-reduction target. Since then guide reaffirmations have been sold or met flat: -9.1% (2026-03-19, initial FY27 guide), -13.6% (2026-06-09), -2.1% (2026-08-27, guide reaffirmed with an EPS miss).
findings.why_not_priced: Both facts are public. But the stock has fallen about 23% from its $26.90 high and 10% in 20 days while this cash was being paid, so the price is not trading on it. If it were priced, TITN would have held its rally alongside a capital-investment index at a one-year high rather than tracking corn lower. Nobody quantifies the payment's effect on Titan's Q4 order book until management speaks on the 24th.
findings.independence: USDA/farmdoc on the payment size (https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2026/10/2025-final-arc-plc-payments.html, 2026-10-13). A Farm Progress piece dated 2026-11-07 says rising commodity prices are reviving equipment demand and auction activity has jumped (https://www.farmprogress.com/farming-equipment/buy-now-or-wait-equipment-prices-won-t-get-cheaper; date per search snippet). This is a proxy: neither Titan nor CNH has confirmed a Q4 order effect.

findings.finding: December CBOT corn fell from a contract high around $5.38 on 2026-08-28 (Pro Farmer) to $4.355 on 2026-11-18 (UkrAgroConsult), about -19%, after two months of speculative fund liquidation. On the 2026-08-27 call management and an analyst leaned on rising corn (near $5.50 cited) as the reason calendar 2026 'could be the bottom' and farmers could return to profitability. That supports narrative is now weaker into any year-end or FY28 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release cites crop prices as the driver of a reaction. The stock rallied about 32% after the August print alongside the corn rally and has given back about 23% since its $26.90 high as corn fell.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the 23% drawdown from the high is the visible pricing. What is not priced is whether management walks back its 'bottom of the cycle' language on the call; consensus FY EPS still sits at the guide midpoint, so analysts have not cut on corn. Sized small, and against the skew (calls bid).
findings.independence: The late-August level is from a different source, Pro Farmer 2026-08-28 (https://www.profarmer.com/pro-farmer-max/market-snapshot/market-snapshot-rally-extends-late-week-trade). Proxy only: macro-to-company transmission.

findings.finding: Consensus Q3 revenue of $541-556M (FY about $2.13B) sits at or above the top of what Titan's own segment guide implies. FY26 segments were Ag $1,557.8M, Construction $311.0M, Europe $377.7M, Australia $180.5M. Applying the reaffirmed guide (Ag -15 to -20%, Construction +5 to +10%, Europe -30 to -40%, Australia +15 to +20%) gives FY27 of $2.01-2.15B. Less H1 of $1,018.8M, and with Q3 and Q4 'pretty balanced', that implies Q3 around $520-540M even at the ends of the ranges management leaned to. Against $644.5M a year ago, Q3 at that level is down 16-19%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 FY27, revenue of $496.4M beat consensus but EPS of -$0.40 missed -$0.35, and the stock fell 2.1%. In Q3 FY26, a revenue beat with a surprise profit moved it +18.5%. Revenue alone has not carried the reaction; EPS and the outlook have.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote consensus and the guide side by side without doing the segment arithmetic. If the gap were priced, consensus would sit near $530M rather than $552M. It is an inference from the company's own guide, and Titan beat revenue in Q2 (management said H1 ran ahead on early presold factory shipments), so it is kept small.
findings.independence: The segment guide is in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001409171/000162828026059170/afy27q2ex991earningsrelease.htm). The FY consensus of $2.13B sitting above the top of the range is also noted by the 2026-11-16 finviz preview (https://finviz.com/news/423386/titan-machinerys-rally-meets-a-tough-second-half-ag-test-as-europe-weakens). It shares the guide document with the industry-data finding below, which points the other way on ag volume.

findings.finding: Industry retail during Titan's Aug-Oct quarter ran at or better than its guide of about -20% for H2 domestic ag equipment. AEM September: US tractors -16.4%, 4WD -20.2%, combines -10.9%. AEM October: tractors -0.5%, 4WD +7.7%, 2WD >100hp +3.2%, combines -9.6%. CNH's Q3 (Jul-Sep) North America: >140hp tractors -5%, combines -13%. October's high-horsepower stabilisation is the category Titan sells most.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ag same-store sales of -8.4% in Q2 were better than the guide, and the stock fell 2.1% on the EPS miss. The Ag line has not on its own moved a print.
findings.why_not_priced: AEM monthly data is public, but previews (finviz 2026-11-16) frame H2 as a 'tough second-half ag test' at -20% and do not mention October's turn in high-horsepower units. Management attributed part of the -20% to timing (presold units shipped early into H1), which industry retail does not see.
findings.independence: CNH Q3 2026 release and presentation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000020/ex991q326.htm, 2026-11-09). AEM September via Farm Progress (https://www.farmprogress.com/tv-and-radio/farm-equipment-sales-keep-sliding-as-farmers-hold-onto-older-machinery, 2026-10-23). Industry proxy, not Titan's own number.

findings.finding: Q3 FY26's comparison carried items that do not repeat. Ag pre-tax income of $6.1M included a $3.7M partial accrual for manufacturer incentives. Europe earned $3.5M pre-tax on $117.0M revenue (+77.8% ex-FX, driven by Romanian EU-stimulus sales) and now runs at a loss ($-1.3M in Q2) with FY revenue guided -30 to -40%, Germany largely wound down ($11M in FY27 against $53.9M). So the year-over-year EPS line (+$0.05 to about -$0.08) will read as a deterioration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 FY27, Europe's swing to a loss accompanied the EPS miss and a -2.1% move.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced and inside guidance: consensus EPS of -$0.08 against +$0.05 a year ago already reflects it. Sized near zero, filed for completeness.
findings.independence: The Q2 FY27 release gives the Europe and Germany figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001409171/000162828026059170/afy27q2ex991earningsrelease.htm).

findings.finding: Titan's primary supplier CNH (Q3, 2026-11-09) cut ag dealer inventories by about $100M in the quarter and said 'improving cycle indicators in North America reinforce our confidence'. It narrowed its FY ag EBIT margin to 5.1-5.4%, and part of its EBIT was IEEPA tariff refunds. Less factory push into dealers supports Titan's inventory and floorplan reduction, the line its +18.5% Q3 FY26 reaction turned on. Other peers were mixed: AGCO cut its outlook (2026-10-29) and Titan International's ag sales fell 12% with a soft Q4 guide (2026-10-29).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The inventory-reduction line drove the +18.5% at Q3 FY26 (target raised to $150M) and the reaction to Q4 FY26, when $206M cumulative was achieved and the stock fell 9.1% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: CNH's dealer-destock figure is in its presentation, not in TITN previews, which discuss Titan's inventory only as a $931.5M July figure. If priced, the stock would not have fallen alongside the CNH print week. It is a counterparty read, not Titan's own number, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: AGCO Q3 (https://www.agnavigator.com/Article/2026/10/29/agco-q3-results-highlight-global-market-challenges-amid-stressed-farm-economics/) and Titan International Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000899751/000089975126000084/q326earningsreleaseex99.htm) point the other way, so peers are mixed.

outside_window.finding: Deere reports fiscal Q4 2026 and gives its first FY27 outlook before the open on 2026-11-25, one session after TITN's exit window closes at the 2026-11-24 close. Its large-ag outlook is the main sector read-through and will not be seen by this trade.

The ABARES December crop report (due 2026-12-01) follows a September forecast of South Australia +24% (11.3 Mt) and Western Australia -16%. That is relevant to Titan's Australia segment (guided +15-20%) but lands after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR submissions since 2026-08-01: only the 10-Q (2026-09-03), the Q2 8-K, and three Schedule 13G filings (2026-10-23, 2026-11-16 x2); no 8-K other than earnings, no Form 4 insider trades (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001409171.json)
Titan-specific IEEPA tariff refund: none found; peers CNH, AGCO, Kubota and Komatsu booked refunds, but Titan is a dealer and not evidently the importer of record
A cause for the -8% from $22.57 (2026-11-16) to $20.70 (2026-11-23): no company news found; the likeliest explanation is the corn slide, filed above
Analyst actions in the last month: an AAII note mentions one unnamed upgrade in October; the dates on Baird and Northland targets could not be confirmed
A detailed Q3-vs-Q4 split from the Q2 call: only 'Q4 a little stronger than Q3, but pretty balanced'

baseline_tension: Mixed. The positive farm-cash finding agrees with the skew (calls bid, -11). The corn and consensus-vs-guide negatives agree with the 20-day run-down and the last three sold prints, and they cut against the skew, so they are kept small. p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy): ARC/PLC and sentiment finding cut from +1.5 to +1.2; still filed.
Lesson 7 (sign against strong skew -11, upside paid): corn finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lessons 5 and 6 (inference; bar has two roughly agreeing sources but Titan beat revenue in Q2): consensus-above-guide finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 6 (inside what the company guided): prior-year comp items cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; last three prints sold): no further cut to findings; p_up held at 51 rather than leaning on the positives.
Industry-data and CNH findings left unchanged.
